rationale: The Chlordane row at Outfall 001 in Part I Section A does not establish any enforceable numeric effluent discharge limit: all six limit columns (30-day average, daily maximum, and 7-day average for both mass and concentration) are explicitly marked N/A, unlike parameters such as Cyanide that carry numeric limits in the same columns. It does establish a required monitoring and reporting obligation at the stated frequency: the row assigns Report in the final limit-column position, 1/Quarter measurement frequency, and Grab sample type, matching the same N/A/Report pattern used for adjacent pollutants (Cadmium, Aldrin, Toxaphene, etc.) and contrasting with limit-bearing rows. Table headers separate the six effluent-limit columns from measurement frequency and sample type, so Report and 1/Quarter are monitoring obligations rather than limit values. The answer to why_demanded is therefore (b), not (a) or (c).
